Would you like to lead and further develop the Finance function at Denmark’s largest refinery? Kalundborg Refinery is seeking an experienced Head of Finance to combine hands-on operational finance leadership with strategic influence on site performance.

The high requirements for safety, operational reliability and regulatory compliance in a critical industrial environment require strong financial leadership, clear governance and the ability to create effective collaboration across site operations and Group functions.

Kalundborg Refinery is critical infrastructure within Denmark’s energy supply system and accounts for more than 15% of the country’s total energy consumption. Since January 2022, the refinery has been part of Klesch Group and operates alongside a sister site in Heide, Germany, and a recently acquired refinery in Gelsenkirchen, also in Germany. Under Klesch Group ownership, Kalundborg Refinery continues to operate with an uncompromising focus on safe and reliable operations, operational excellence and long-term value creation.

As Head of Finance, you will lead the full Finance function at Kalundborg Refinery and act as the primary financial steward and business partner to the Site Managing Director. You will be closely connected to Group and report to the Group CFO, ensuring alignment with Group finance standards, controls and reporting. As a member of the Leadership Team, you will contribute to the Company’s overall business strategy and take responsibility for both day-to-day operations and strategic initiatives across Finance.

You will have overall leadership and management responsibility for Controlling, Accounting, budgeting and Tax in Kalundborg. Your key responsibilities include:

• Ensuring effective and efficient management and execution of all finance-related matters.

• Ensuring operational excellence within Finance and compliance with applicable requirements and Company policies.

• Overseeing quarterly financial reporting and the preparation of annual financial statements, ensuring clean, credible and on-time reporting with no material control gaps.

• Overseeing and monitoring relevant direct and indirect tax matters.

• Preparing monthly management information for the shareholder and senior leadership team. Ensuring an effective and timely monthly financial close.

• Driving the budgeting process in Kalundborg with close coordination with project managers and Group.

• Supporting the management of structured finance arrangements, including preparation for and participation in bank calls, liquidity planning and liquidity monitoring.

• Leading and developing the Finance team, strengthening KPI dashboard reporting and building clear succession visibility.

The right candidate has:

• A degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics or a related field, combined with 8–12+ years of finance experience in multinational and manufacturing or industrial environments.

• A track record of leading a Finance team of comparable size, approximately 10–15 employees, at plant or site level.

• Strong command of IFRS and experience with financial reporting; consolidated reporting experience is an advantage.

• Experience with cost accounting, standard costing, capex appraisal, ERP systems — preferably SAP or equivalent — and advanced financial modelling and analysis.

• Fluency in a Scandinavian language and professional proficiency in English.

• The ability to operate confidently as a peer to plant operations leadership and manage stakeholders effectively across a dual reporting structure.

• Demonstrates dynamism and a continuous drive for results.

• Attention to detail and ability to present complex matters in a simple way.

• A demonstrated ability to develop and retain an engaged Finance team, communicate difficult financial truths with commercial tact and build strong functional capability.

The position is based in Kalundborg, Denmark. Travel (app. 2 days per month) is to be expected.

Would you like to know more?

Please review the detailed Assignment Brief before contacting Mercuri Urval for a confidential discussion with director Thomas Gajhede, MU (+45 2084 1030).

Aarhus Airport is hiring an Analyst (Route Development & Marketing)

Aarhus Airport is growing – this year we are seeing a record number of passengers enjoy the very best customer experience of Denmark’s fastest growing airport while traveling to and from a widening number of destinations with our airline and tour operator partners. Can you see the next new opportunity and identify the latest trends to influence where customers will fly and how they get there? We will be welcoming more partners, destinations and guests, making use of ever-developing airport amenities that require planning, analysis and performance monitoring. To help us do so, we are looking for a new and talented colleague to join the strategic team that leads our route development, marketing and communications work. Energetically researching, monitoring, analysing and determining the data and insight that powers our planning and harnessing of valuable air capacity for Aarhus and the region, if you would like to be part of the team that shapes this connectivity strategy for the Nordic region’s fifth most populous metro area, to bring millions of customers to thousands of flights that service Aarhus Airport now and in the years to come, we want to hear from you.

Our ideal Analyst will be able to join as soon as possible and get to work on carrying-out market analysis of both existing and new potential routes, with both existing and future airline and tour operator partners. This opportunity is located at our brand-new offices at Aarhus Airport and will be an integral part of our team-spirited wider airport family, working across the organisation as required.

In this position your primary areas of responsibility will include:

• Analysing existing routes, potential routes and aviation market data, supporting work in growing passenger throughput, generating business cases and providing valuable data to the Route Development, Marketing & Communications team

• Helping attract and win new airline services, tour operators and air freight providers among other business development opportunities by way of sharp and investigative analysis

• Work astutely with market intelligence and data – from reporting, analysing, market-sizing and trend development, to identifying, researching and underpinning new business opportunity by smartly applying business acumen

• Develop a grasp and detailed understanding of population dynamics, socio-economic, migration and immigration as well as regional economic trends across Denmark and applicable international communities, as well as trade and tourism

• Using both new and available data and analytical methodology, support the commercial activity, sales, marketing and communication initiatives of the organisation

• Produce, research and maintain analytical and insight tools to help optimally showcase Aarhus Airport’s market, regional economy and destination assets

• Support the knowledge-building of AAR’s work in economic, aviation and wider industry trends

• Support work with stakeholders and business partners from around the industry and region including tourism partners, corporate customers, airlines and tour operator partners

• Assist with applicable project management and business development by way of competent planning, modelling, budgeting and forecasting

• Assist in commercial calculations, analysis and negotiations with management and leadership, in pursuit of incremental revenue sustainability and asset optimisation

• Co-operate closely with marketing, communications, administration, customer service and operational colleagues

• Attend and support airline and tour operator negotiations as required, including attendance of industry conferences, conventions and exhibitions. The role involves some international travel which should appeal to your general wanderlust and passion for travel, tourism and/or aviation

The right candidate will, among other attributes, demonstrate that they have:

• Strong skill sets in analytical, business and/or commercial arena and ideally some international work experience, or a very significant interest in this field. Perhaps you have worked in travel already or are keen to do so, maybe an interest in airport, airline and the travel sector in general

• A business degree of relevance with a lean towards statistical, data and analytical strengths, possibly within business, economics, marketing, communications or another commercial discipline

• Fluency in English, perhaps a Scandinavian language too. Additional languages are an advantage

• A head for numbers, strong IT and excellent interpersonal communication skills are a must. Fully competent in excel, powerpoint, other IT suites and data tools, where thinking outside of the box, challenging assumptions with evidence and insight, above all being inquisitive and solution-oriented are second nature

• The ability to work confidently and in a structured way with extensive data material and in detail, producing meaningful analysis, reports, proposals and delivering valuable insight to colleagues and decision-makers. At the same time you are able to work independently and as part of a team, tie dynamic data and insight together and present complex data in an attractive way, visually and verbally

• The ability to gain security clearance from the Danish Police, hold a valid passport and have or obtain the right to live and work in Aarhus, Denmark is a minimum requirement.

Aarhus Airport offers a range of benefits in line with qualifications and experience. We have towering ambitions for the future and invite you to join us if the above snapshot is a fit and you are keen to contribute in building the region’s future international connectivity, and the potential to develop your career with us excites you. We are an equal opportunities employer and an organisation that likes to stand out from the crowd, we thrive on excellence and diversity within our team regardless of background, ethnicity, gender or sexual orientation. We expect the review of applications and interviews to be ongoing until the position is filled, and encourage you to reach out as soon as possible if the opportunity resonates.

We look forward to receiving your CV and covering letter with an indication of salary expectations via the application link on our website. If you have any questions, feel free to contact us by email at dsu@aar.dk

jobs.occupation: PhD Position at the Department of Law, University of Southern Denmark (SDU) Religious Education, Legal Consciousness and Social Cohesion in Post-Imperial Islamic Societies
jobs.description:
The Department of Law at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) invites applications for a fully funded three-year PhD position within the Horizon Europe Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network MINARET – Islamic Legal Cultures in Post-Imperial Contexts. Employment is expected to begin September 1, 2027, or by agreement.

The successful candidate will be enrolled in the PhD School at SDU Business School and the Faculty of Social Sciences and employed at the Department of Law, University of Southern Denmark.

 

About the MINARET Doctoral Network

MINARET is an international doctoral network funded through the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA). The network investigates how Islamic legal cultures shape governance, citizenship, institutions and everyday legal practices across post-imperial societies.

The programme brings together universities and non-academic partners across Europe, North Africa, Central Asia and Southeast Asia. Doctoral candidates will receive interdisciplinary training, international supervision and extensive mobility opportunities.

Further information about the network is available at MINARET website.

 

Project Description

This doctoral project examines how constitutional and legal frameworks governing religious education shape citizenship, legal consciousness and social cohesion in Indonesia and Morocco.

The project investigates how constitutional values, religious identities and civic norms are translated into educational practices and everyday experiences of citizenship. Particular attention is paid to how religious education influences democratic participation, social integration and perceptions of rights, duties and belonging.

The project contributes to research on legal consciousness, sociology of law, citizenship studies and comparative constitutionalism. Through comparative empirical research in Indonesia and Morocco, the doctoral candidate will analyse how educational institutions function as sites where legal norms, religious values and civic identities intersect.

The candidate is expected to develop an original research design within the overall framework of the project.

 

Host Institution

The position is based at the Department of Law, University of Southern Denmark, Denmark.

The Department of Law is part of the Faculty of Social Sciences and hosts a vibrant interdisciplinary environment within sociology of law, legal anthropology, human rights and comparative legal studies.

The successful candidate will become part of the department’s research environment as well as the international MINARET doctoral network.

More information about our PhD programme is available at the department’s website. On the website, you will also find the department’s qualifications criteria. The programme is provided by the PhD School at SDU Business School and the Faculty of Social Sciences who offer further information on their website.

 

Supervision

The doctoral candidate will be supervised by:

• 
Professor Ole Hammerslev (University of Southern Denmark) (principal supervisor)

• 
Co-supervisor from MINARET consortium

Additional mentoring and supervision will be provided through the MINARET network.

 

Fieldwork and Mobility

The project includes substantial international mobility.

The doctoral candidate is expected to conduct fieldwork in:

• 
Indonesia

• 
Morocco

 

In addition, the candidate will undertake two secondments within the MINARET network:

• 
one academic secondment at a partner university;

• 
one non-academic secondment with a relevant partner organisation.

 

Participation in network-wide training events, workshops, summer schools and conferences is mandatory.

 

Tasks and Responsibilities

The successful candidate will:

• 
conduct independent doctoral research within the project framework;

• 
participate actively in the MINARET doctoral network;

• 
undertake international fieldwork and secondments;

• 
complete PhD courses and training activities;

• 
contribute to the research environment at the Department of Law;

• 
participate in teaching and related activities in accordance with Danish PhD regulations.

 

Eligibility Requirements

Applicants must hold a relevant master’s degree (or equivalent) in law, sociology, political science, anthropology, religious studies, education, or a related social science discipline.

Applicants must meet the admission requirements of the PhD School at SDU Business School and the Faculty of Social Sciences, SDU, which you can learn more about on the PhD School’s website. 

Applicants must also meet requirements in accordance with the MSCA Doctoral Network:

• 
applicants must not already hold a doctoral degree;

• 
applicants must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Denmark for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately preceding the recruitment date.

Excellent English language skills are required.

 

Desired Qualifications

Preference will be given to applicants with documented experience or interest in one or more of the following areas:

• 
sociology of law;

• 
legal consciousness;

• 
citizenship studies;

• 
religion and law;

• 
Islamic legal cultures;

• 
qualitative and comparative research methods;

• 
fieldwork-based research.

 

Knowledge of Arabic, Bahasa Indonesia, French or other relevant languages is an advantage but not a requirement.

 

Assessment Criteria

Applicants will be assessed on:

• 
academic qualifications (please consult the guidelines for recognizing merit at the Department of Law);

• 
quality and feasibility of the proposed research project;

• 
methodological competencies;

• 
motivation and suitability for international and interdisciplinary research;

• 
ability to contribute to the objectives of the MINARET doctoral network.

 

We Offer

The position offers:

• 
Three years of full-time employment as a PhD fellow at SDU;

• 
enrolment in an internationally recognised PhD programme;

• 
participation in a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network;

• 
international supervision and training;

• 
research mobility and secondments;

• 
competitive salary and employment conditions in accordance with Danish regulations and MSCA provisions.

 

Contact information

For more information about the department and the position, please contact Head of Department, Ole Hammerslev, ohv@sam.sdu.dk. 

 

Terms of employment      
The applicant will be employed in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) for academics in the state sector, including the associated circular on the job structure for academic staff at universities and the regulations for PhD students as described therein.

Employment as a PhD student is subject to the circular of 20 December 2021, on the agreement for academics in the state sector – Appendix 5, protocol on PhD students.

The person employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a self-organiser.

Salary and employment terms

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements.

As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process.

SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary.

 

The assessment and evaluation process

Shortlisting may be used in the assessment process. Please note that only shortlisted applicants will receive an assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU.

Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee and the shortlisted applicants will receive the part of the evaluation that concerns them. The committee may request additional information, and if so, it is the responsibility of the applicants to provide the necessary material.

Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. 

 

Application   

 

The application must include the following:

•   Motivated application
•   Detailed Curriculum vitae (educational and work history should be specified by month and year)
•   A certified copy of your master’s degree certificate, including transcripts of all examination results – alternatively, the expected date to finish the master’s degree. Foreign diplomas that are not in Norwegian, Swedish or English must be accompanied by a translation into Danish or English, as well as a translation of the official description of the marking scale used. 
•   An application form (is available here)
•   A project description (max 5 pages of 2,400 characters each, including spaces, notes, appendices, bibliography etc.). The guidelines for preparing a PhD project proposal for the Department of Law are available here.
•   An abstract of the project description of no more than 250 words
•   Publications, if any – however, no more than two. If one of the attached publications is a master thesis, only the problem formulation and the conclusion should be attached, not the entire thesis.
•   Information on teaching experience or other forms of academic communication.

Documents which are not in Danish, Norwegian or Swedish must be translated into English. SDU may discard applications which are incomplete regarding the above-mentioned criteria without further notice. All documents must be in pdf format, no more than 5 MB per file. 

Documents should not contain a CPR number (civil registration number) – in this case, the CPR number must be crossed out.

Applicants are encouraged to read the information "How to apply" before applying. If you experience technical problems when uploading the application, please contact hcm-support@sdu.dk. 

UPLOAD GUIDE: Motivated application should be uploaded as ‘Cover letter’, Curriculum Vitae should be uploaded as ‘Resume’. All other documents should be uploaded as ‘Miscellaneous documents’. 

 

The application deadline is January 31, 2027, 23.59 CET/CEST.

 Applications must be submitted electronically using the link "Apply now" on our website.

The University of Southern Denmark wishes to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position.

 

About SDU

The University of Southern Denmark was established to create value for and with society. Whether our contributions come in the form of excellent research, innovative solutions, education or learning, we must make a positive difference to society and contribute to a sustainable future. We do this by cultivating talents and creating the best environments for research and learning. It is therefore crucial that SDU retains, develops and recruits talent. At the same time, we need to ensure consistently high quality in all our activities – and we can only do that with the right people. The University’s researchers, lecturers, students, managers and technical/administrative staff are the foundation of our success.
